title: EasyACIM: An End-to-End Automated Analog CIM with Synthesizable Architecture and Agile Design Space Exploration
problem: Current Analog Computing-in-Memory (ACIM) designs suffer from unscalable topologies and require heavy manual design effort. This limits application scenarios and increases time-to-market for ACIM systems.
motivation: ACIM is an emerging architecture for efficient AI inference at the edge, and automating its design can accelerate adoption and enable broader application coverage.
method: EasyACIM provides end-to-end automated ACIM design through a synthesizable architecture that accepts array size and customized cell libraries as inputs and generates complete layouts automatically. The framework employs a multi-objective genetic algorithm (MOGA) to explore the design space and identify high-quality ACIM solutions across various design specifications and application scenarios.
key_novelty: Synthesizable ACIM architecture combined with automated end-to-end generation and MOGA-based design space exploration to enable scalable and agile ACIM design without manual intervention.
contributions: End-to-end automated ACIM design framework eliminating manual design efforts
Synthesizable ACIM architecture enabling scalability and automation
MOGA-based design space explorer for obtaining high-quality solutions across multiple objectives
Demonstration of wide design space with competitive performance versus state-of-the-art ACIM designs

metrics.other: Competitive performance compared to state-of-the-art ACIMs; wide design space exploration

limitations: Not discussed in abstract; specific performance metrics and comparison data not provided.
primary_theme: Automated analog computing-in-memory design and synthesis
